name: Greek Words 301–400
description: Common Greek nouns, pronouns, adjectives and adverbs, numbers 301–400 on the frequency list. Nouns come with their article, plural and genitive; adjectives with their feminine and neuter forms.

cards.definition: A picture taken with a camera.

examples.text: Μπορείτε να μας βγάλετε μια φωτογραφία;
examples.translation: Could you take a photo of us?
I like old photographs.

cards.notes: Βγάζω φωτογραφία = to take a photo.

cards.definition: How big or small something is.

examples.translation: What size do you wear?
Do you have it in a bigger size?

cards.definition: A recording of moving pictures.

examples.translation: She sent me a funny video.
I watch videos on my phone.

cards.notes: Never changes form.

cards.definition: What something is about; a matter to deal with.

examples.translation: Let's change the subject.
No problem!

cards.definition: A quantity, especially of money.

examples.translation: What's the total amount?

examples.text: Πλήρωσα ένα μεγάλο ποσό για το ενοίκιο.
examples.translation: I paid a large sum for the rent.

cards.definition: One side of a sheet of paper in a book; a web page.

examples.text: Ανοίξτε το βιβλίο στη σελίδα δέκα.
examples.translation: Open the book at page ten.
The book has three hundred pages.

cards.notes: A website is η ιστοσελίδα.

cards.definition: Work or a job; a piece of work to do.

examples.text: Πρέπει να τελειώσω μια εργασία για το πανεπιστήμιο.
examples.translation: I have to finish an assignment for university.
She's looking for work.

cards.notes: More formal than δουλειά.

cards.definition: A paper showing that you paid; evidence.

examples.translation: Can I have a receipt?
There's no proof at all.

cards.definition: A business organisation.

examples.translation: I work for a big company.

examples.text: Η εταιρεία έχει γραφεία στην Αθήνα.
examples.translation: The company has offices in Athens.

cards.definition: Painting, music and other creative work; a skill.

examples.translation: I'm interested in modern art.
Cooking is an art.

cards.definition: A building for plays; the art of acting.

examples.translation: Shall we go to the theatre on Saturday?

examples.text: Το αρχαίο θέατρο της Επιδαύρου είναι εντυπωσιακό.
examples.translation: The ancient theatre of Epidaurus is impressive.

cards.definition: A place where things are sold (formal word).

examples.text: Τα καταστήματα είναι κλειστά την Κυριακή.
examples.translation: The shops are closed on Sundays.

examples.text: Το κατάστημα βρίσκεται στον πρώτο όροφο.
examples.translation: The store is on the first floor.

cards.notes: More formal than το μαγαζί; used on signs and in official language.

cards.definition: Moving your body to music.

examples.translation: We like Greek dances.
Shall we go dancing tonight?

cards.notes: Χορεύω = to dance.

cards.definition: The money you are paid regularly for your work.

examples.text: Ο μισθός μου δεν είναι πολύ μεγάλος.
examples.translation: My salary isn't very big.

examples.text: Παίρνουμε τον μισθό στο τέλος του μήνα.
examples.translation: We get our salary at the end of the month.

cards.definition: A game in which two teams kick a ball.

examples.translation: Do you watch football?
We play football every Sunday.

cards.notes: Usually no plural.

cards.definition: A round object used in games.

examples.translation: Throw me the ball!

examples.text: Τα παιδιά παίζουν μπάλα στην αυλή.
examples.translation: The children are playing football in the yard.

cards.notes: Παίζω μπάλα = to play football (informal).

cards.definition: A list of what you have to pay; a bank or online account.

examples.translation: The bill, please.
I opened a bank account.

cards.definition: A good moment to do something; a cheap offer.

examples.text: Είναι μια μεγάλη ευκαιρία για σένα.
examples.translation: It's a great opportunity for you.
This price is a bargain!

cards.definition: Money or benefit you get from something.

examples.text: Η εταιρεία είχε μεγάλα κέρδη φέτος.
examples.translation: The company made big profits this year.

examples.text: Δεν το κάνω για το κέρδος.
examples.translation: I'm not doing it for the money.

cards.definition: A test of knowledge; a medical check.

examples.translation: I have exams tomorrow.

examples.text: Ο γιατρός θέλει να κάνω εξετάσεις αίματος.
examples.translation: The doctor wants me to have blood tests.

cards.notes: Often plural: οι εξετάσεις.

cards.definition: The amount you have to pay for something.

examples.text: Το κόστος ζωής είναι πολύ υψηλό.
examples.translation: The cost of living is very high.

examples.text: Ποιο είναι το κόστος της επισκευής;
examples.translation: How much will the repair cost?

cards.notes: Κοστίζει = it costs.

cards.definition: A group of pupils; a school year; tidiness or order.

examples.text: Ο γιος μου πάει στην τρίτη τάξη.
examples.translation: My son is in third grade.

examples.text: Βάλε σε τάξη το δωμάτιό σου.
examples.translation: Tidy up your room.

cards.notes: Εντάξει = OK (literally "in order").

cards.definition: A planned time when people meet.

examples.translation: I have a meeting at ten.
The meeting was cancelled.

cards.definition: The system of money and trade in a country; saving money.

examples.text: Η ελληνική οικονομία στηρίζεται στον τουρισμό.
examples.translation: The Greek economy relies on tourism.
I'm saving up for the holidays.

cards.notes: Οι οικονομίες = savings.

cards.definition: A plant used in cooking or medicine.

examples.text: Η γιαγιά μου μαζεύει βότανα από το βουνό.
examples.translation: My grandmother picks herbs on the mountain.
The food has lots of herbs in it.

cards.notes: Greek kitchen herbs: η ρίγανη (oregano), το θυμάρι (thyme), ο βασιλικός (basil).

cards.definition: A country and its government.

examples.translation: The state has to help.

examples.text: Η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση έχει είκοσι επτά κράτη μέλη.
examples.translation: The European Union has twenty-seven member states.

cards.definition: An old traditional story; a common false belief.

examples.translation: I like Greek myths.
That's a myth, it isn't true.

cards.notes: Η μυθολογία = mythology.

cards.definition: The group of people who run a country.

examples.translation: The government announced new measures.
The new government was sworn in yesterday.

cards.definition: A being believed to have power over the world.

examples.text: Οι αρχαίοι Έλληνες είχαν πολλούς θεούς.
examples.translation: The ancient Greeks had many gods.
My God!

cards.notes: Δόξα τω Θεώ = thank God.

cards.definition: A building for Christian worship; the Church.

examples.translation: They go to church every Sunday.

examples.text: Το χωριό έχει μια μικρή εκκλησία.
examples.translation: The village has a small church.

cards.definition: The head of a country, company or group.

examples.text: Ο Πρόεδρος της Δημοκρατίας επισκέφτηκε την Κρήτη.
examples.translation: The President of the Republic visited Crete.
She's the chair of the association.

cards.notes: The same word is used for a woman, with the feminine article: η πρόεδρος.

cards.definition: Images in your mind while you sleep; a hope.

examples.translation: Sweet dreams!

examples.text: Το όνειρό μου είναι να ζήσω σε ένα νησί.
examples.translation: My dream is to live on an island.

cards.notes: Βλέπω όνειρο = to have a dream.

cards.definition: The activities of government; a plan of action.

examples.text: Δεν μου αρέσει να μιλάω για πολιτική.
examples.translation: I don't like talking about politics.

examples.text: Η εταιρεία έχει νέα πολιτική για τις άδειες.
examples.translation: The company has a new leave policy.

cards.notes: Ο πολιτικός = politician.

cards.definition: The relationship between friends.

examples.translation: Our friendship goes back years.

examples.text: Η φιλία είναι πολύ σημαντική για μένα.
examples.translation: Friendship is very important to me.

cards.definition: The feeling you have when you are afraid.

examples.translation: He's afraid of flying. (literally "has a fear of planes")
He was trembling with fear.

cards.notes: Φοβάμαι = to be afraid.

cards.definition: A rule made by a government.

examples.text: Αυτό είναι αντίθετο με τον νόμο.
examples.translation: That's against the law.
Parliament passed a new law.

cards.notes: Don't confuse it with ο νομός (stress at the end) = prefecture, region.

cards.definition: A damaged place on the body.

examples.translation: The wound is slowly healing.
Clean the wound with water.

cards.definition: Something you are allowed or entitled to.

examples.translation: You have every right to be angry.

examples.text: Τα ανθρώπινα δικαιώματα είναι πολύ σημαντικά.
examples.translation: Human rights are very important.

cards.definition: Something you must have or do.

examples.translation: There's no need.
I need some rest.

cards.notes: Έχω ανάγκη (από) = I need. Σε περίπτωση ανάγκης = in an emergency.

cards.definition: Being free to do what you want.

examples.text: Η ελευθερία του λόγου είναι δικαίωμα.
examples.translation: Freedom of speech is a right.

examples.text: Μου αρέσει η ελευθερία που έχω εδώ.
examples.translation: I like the freedom I have here.

cards.definition: The expression your face makes when you are happy.

examples.translation: She has a wonderful smile.
He welcomed me with a smile.

cards.notes: Χαμογελάω = to smile.

cards.definition: The sound you make when you laugh.

examples.text: Ακούγονταν γέλια από το διπλανό δωμάτιο.
examples.translation: Laughter could be heard from the next room.
We died laughing!

cards.notes: Γελάω = to laugh.

cards.definition: A time without war or fighting.

examples.translation: We all want peace.

examples.text: Η συμφωνία έφερε ειρήνη στην περιοχή.
examples.translation: The agreement brought peace to the region.

cards.notes: Ειρήνη is also a common girl's name.

cards.definition: Something you can hear.

examples.text: Μου αρέσει ο ήχος της θάλασσας.
examples.translation: I like the sound of the sea.
Turn the sound down, please.

cards.definition: A country's armed forces on land.

examples.text: Ο αδερφός μου είναι στον στρατό.
examples.translation: My brother is in the army.

examples.text: Ο στρατός βοήθησε μετά τον σεισμό.
examples.translation: The army helped after the earthquake.

cards.notes: Πάω στρατό = to do military service (compulsory for men in Greece).

cards.definition: Having the colour of lemons.

examples.translation: She's wearing a yellow dress.

examples.text: Τα φύλλα γίνονται κίτρινα το φθινόπωρο.
examples.translation: The leaves turn yellow in autumn.

cards.definition: All the people of a country.

examples.text: Ο ελληνικός λαός είναι πολύ φιλόξενος.
examples.translation: The Greek people are very hospitable.
The people have voted.

cards.notes: Λαϊκός = popular, folk: λαϊκή μουσική = popular/folk music; η λαϊκή = the street market.

cards.definition: Having the colour of a clear sky.

examples.translation: The sky is blue.

examples.text: Η ελληνική σημαία είναι γαλάζια και άσπρη.
examples.translation: The Greek flag is blue and white.

cards.notes: Μπλε = (dark) blue. The Greek flag is called η γαλανόλευκη, "the blue-and-white".

cards.definition: Between black and white in colour.

examples.translation: The sky is grey today.
I bought a grey coat.

cards.notes: Never changes form. Also γκρίζος, γκρίζα, γκρίζο.

cards.definition: People living together in a community.

examples.translation: We live in a multicultural society.
Technology is changing society.

cards.definition: Having the colour of coffee or earth.

examples.translation: He has brown eyes.

examples.text: Θέλω τα καφέ παπούτσια, όχι τα μαύρα.
examples.translation: I want the brown shoes, not the black ones.

cards.notes: Never changes form. Don't confuse it with ο καφές (coffee). Το καφέ is also a café.

cards.definition: A person who legally belongs to a country.

examples.translation: I'm a Greek citizen.
Citizens vote on Sunday.

cards.definition: Pale red in colour.

examples.text: Η κόρη μου θέλει ένα ροζ ποδήλατο.
examples.translation: My daughter wants a pink bike.

examples.text: Ο ουρανός έγινε ροζ στο ηλιοβασίλεμα.
examples.translation: The sky turned pink at sunset.

cards.notes: Never changes form.

cards.definition: The people watching a show; people in general.

examples.translation: The audience applauded.

examples.text: Το μουσείο είναι ανοιχτό στο κοινό.
examples.translation: The museum is open to the public.

cards.notes: As an adjective, κοινός, κοινή, κοινό = common, shared: κοινοί φίλοι = mutual friends.

cards.definition: Coming after the second.

examples.translation: I live on the third floor.

examples.text: Είναι η τρίτη φορά που έρχομαι.
examples.translation: It's the third time I've come.

cards.notes: Η Τρίτη = Tuesday (the third day of the week).

cards.definition: Facts about something.

examples.translation: I need some information.
Where's the information desk?

cards.notes: Usually plural: οι πληροφορίες = information.

cards.definition: Coming at the end; most recent.

examples.translation: It's the last bus.
Lately I've been working a lot.

cards.notes: Τελευταία (adverb) = lately.

cards.definition: New information about something that has happened.

examples.translation: I have some good news!
Did you see the news?

cards.notes: Οι ειδήσεις = the news (on TV or radio).

cards.definition: Coming straight after.

examples.translation: I'm getting off at the next stop.

examples.text: Την επόμενη μέρα φύγαμε για τη Νάξο.
examples.translation: The following day we left for Naxos.

cards.notes: Ο επόμενος! = Next, please!

cards.definition: A year seen as a whole, good or bad.

examples.translation: Happy New Year!
It was a difficult year.

cards.notes: Χρονιά is a year as you live it (a good year, a hard year); for counting years use ο χρόνος / τα χρόνια.

cards.definition: The worldwide computer network.

examples.translation: I found it on the internet.

examples.text: Αγοράζω τα περισσότερα πράγματα από το διαδίκτυο.
examples.translation: I buy most things online.

cards.notes: In everyday speech also το ίντερνετ.

cards.definition: One of the four parts of the year; a period in history.

examples.text: Ποια είναι η αγαπημένη σου εποχή;
examples.translation: What's your favourite season?

examples.text: Εκείνη την εποχή δεν υπήρχαν κινητά.
examples.translation: In those days there were no mobile phones.

cards.notes: The seasons: η άνοιξη, το καλοκαίρι, το φθινόπωρο, ο χειμώνας.

cards.definition: A phone call; an official notice or fine.

examples.translation: I have a missed call.
I got a parking ticket.

cards.definition: The season between winter and summer.

examples.text: Την άνοιξη η Ελλάδα είναι γεμάτη λουλούδια.
examples.translation: In spring Greece is full of flowers.

examples.text: Η άνοιξη είναι η αγαπημένη μου εποχή.
examples.translation: Spring is my favourite season.

cards.notes: Την άνοιξη = in spring.

cards.definition: A group of words that make a statement; an idea put forward.

examples.text: Γράψε μια πρόταση με αυτή τη λέξη.
examples.translation: Write a sentence with this word.

examples.text: Έχω μια πρόταση: πάμε για φαγητό!
examples.translation: I have a suggestion: let's go out to eat!

cards.notes: Πρόταση γάμου = marriage proposal.

cards.definition: The season between summer and winter.

examples.translation: Schools open in autumn.

examples.text: Μου αρέσουν τα χρώματα του φθινοπώρου.
examples.translation: I like the colours of autumn.

cards.notes: Το φθινόπωρο = in autumn.

cards.definition: The middle of the day.

examples.translation: We eat at two in the afternoon.
It's very hot at midday.

cards.notes: In Greece το μεσημέρι covers roughly 12–4 pm, the time for lunch and a rest.

cards.definition: A piece of writing.

examples.text: Διάβασε το κείμενο και απάντησε στις ερωτήσεις.
examples.translation: Read the text and answer the questions.
I translated the text into English.

cards.definition: The part of the day between midday and evening.

examples.translation: See you in the afternoon.
Every afternoon I go running.

cards.notes: Το απόγευμα = in the afternoon (roughly 4–8 pm).

cards.definition: Physical activity and games; sport in general.

examples.text: Ο αθλητισμός κάνει καλό στην υγεία.
examples.translation: Sport is good for your health.

examples.text: Ασχολείται με τον αθλητισμό από μικρός.
examples.translation: He's been into sport since he was young.

cards.notes: Ο αθλητής / η αθλήτρια = athlete. Το άθλημα = a sport.

cards.definition: A short rest from work, school or a show.

examples.translation: Let's take a break.

examples.text: Στο διάλειμμα τα παιδιά παίζουν στην αυλή.
examples.translation: At break time the children play in the yard.

cards.definition: Things you wear.

examples.translation: I have to wash the clothes.
I bought new clothes.

cards.notes: Usually plural.

cards.definition: A sports competition; a fight for something.

examples.translation: Did you watch the match yesterday?
Life is a struggle.

cards.notes: Οι Ολυμπιακοί Αγώνες = the Olympic Games.

cards.definition: Something you wear on your foot.

examples.translation: How much are these shoes?
Take your shoes off.

cards.definition: Winning a game, fight or competition.

examples.text: Η ομάδα μας γιορτάζει τη νίκη.
examples.translation: Our team is celebrating the win.
It was a big victory.

cards.notes: Νικάω = to win, to beat. Νίκη is also a girl's name.

cards.definition: A piece of clothing with buttons and a collar.

examples.translation: He's wearing a white shirt.
I have to iron the shirts.

cards.definition: Achieving what you wanted; something very popular.

examples.translation: Good luck! (for an exam, a new job…)
The concert was a great success.

cards.definition: Clothing covering each leg separately.

examples.translation: I'm wearing black trousers.

examples.text: Αυτό το παντελόνι μού είναι μεγάλο.
examples.translation: These trousers are too big for me.

cards.notes: Singular in Greek: ένα παντελόνι = a pair of trousers.

cards.definition: A one-piece garment for women and girls.

examples.translation: What a beautiful dress!

examples.text: Θα φορέσω το κόκκινο φόρεμα στον γάμο.
examples.translation: I'll wear the red dress to the wedding.

cards.definition: Not achieving what you wanted.

examples.translation: The film was a failure.
We learn from our failures.

cards.notes: Opposite: επιτυχία.

cards.definition: A piece of clothing that hangs from the waist.

examples.translation: She's wearing a long skirt.

examples.text: Αυτή η φούστα είναι πολύ κοντή.
examples.translation: This skirt is very short.

cards.definition: The possibility of harm.

examples.translation: Caution, danger!

examples.text: Η ζωή του είναι σε κίνδυνο.
examples.translation: His life is in danger.

cards.notes: Επικίνδυνος = dangerous.

cards.definition: Something you wear on your head.

examples.translation: Put a hat on, the sun is strong.

examples.text: Ξέχασα το καπέλο μου στην παραλία.
examples.translation: I left my hat at the beach.

cards.definition: Being safe; protection; an insurance policy.

examples.text: Η ασφάλεια των παιδιών είναι το πιο σημαντικό.
examples.translation: The children's safety is what matters most.
Do you have insurance for the car?

cards.notes: Ζώνη ασφαλείας = seatbelt. Also a (electrical) fuse.

cards.definition: Something you carry things in.

examples.text: Τα κλειδιά είναι στην τσάντα μου.
examples.translation: The keys are in my bag.
Would you like a bag?

cards.definition: Food eaten at one time, such as lunch.

examples.text: Το πρωινό είναι το πιο σημαντικό γεύμα της ημέρας.
examples.translation: Breakfast is the most important meal of the day.
The price includes two meals.

cards.notes: More formal than φαγητό.

cards.definition: Work done for customers; a public office.

examples.text: Η υπηρεσία στο ξενοδοχείο ήταν εξαιρετική.
examples.translation: The service at the hotel was excellent.
Service is included in the price.

cards.notes: Δημόσια υπηρεσία = public service.

cards.definition: The first meal of the day.

examples.translation: What do you have for breakfast?

examples.text: Το πρωινό σερβίρεται από τις επτά ως τις δέκα.
examples.translation: Breakfast is served from seven to ten.

cards.notes: Also the adjective πρωινός, πρωινή, πρωινό = morning. Τα πρωινά = in the mornings.

cards.definition: Something made or grown to be sold.

examples.translation: I only buy Greek products.

examples.text: Αυτό το προϊόν είναι σε προσφορά.
examples.translation: This product is on offer.

cards.definition: The meal eaten in the middle of the day.

examples.translation: What's for lunch?
We have lunch at two.

cards.notes: Short for μεσημεριανό φαγητό.

cards.definition: The meal eaten in the evening.

examples.translation: What are we having for dinner?
Dinner is at nine.

cards.notes: Short for βραδινό φαγητό. More formal: το δείπνο.

cards.definition: A person who buys something or uses a service.

examples.translation: The shop has a lot of customers.
The customer is always right.

cards.definition: A flat dish for food; a prepared food.

examples.translation: Who's going to wash the dishes?

examples.text: Ποιο είναι το πιο γνωστό πιάτο της Κρήτης;
examples.translation: What's the best-known dish of Crete?

cards.definition: How good or bad something is.

examples.text: Αυτό το ύφασμα είναι καλής ποιότητας.
examples.translation: This fabric is good quality.

examples.text: Προτιμώ την ποιότητα από την ποσότητα.
examples.translation: I prefer quality to quantity.

cards.definition: A container made of glass for drinks.

examples.translation: Put the glasses on the table.
I broke a glass.

cards.notes: Glass as a material is το γυαλί.

cards.definition: Knowledge from doing something; an event you lived through.

examples.text: Έχεις εμπειρία σε αυτή τη δουλειά;
examples.translation: Do you have experience in this kind of work?
It was a wonderful experience.

cards.definition: A tool with a blade for cutting.

examples.translation: Can you give me a knife?
Careful, the knife is very sharp.

cards.definition: A thick liquid used in cooking; in Greece usually olive oil.

examples.text: Η Κρήτη έχει το καλύτερο λάδι.
examples.translation: Crete has the best olive oil.
Put a little oil on the salad.

cards.notes: Λάδι on its own usually means olive oil (το ελαιόλαδο).

cards.definition: What you know or have learned.

examples.translation: He knows a lot about history.
Knowledge is power.

cards.notes: Often plural: οι γνώσεις = knowledge, skills.

cards.definition: A food made from milk.

examples.text: Η φέτα είναι το πιο γνωστό ελληνικό τυρί.
examples.translation: Feta is the best-known Greek cheese.
Do you want cheese on your pasta?
